title: Agentic-Teacher: An Agentic Data Engine for Failure-Driven VLA Post-Training
why: A-type teacher-harness for failure-driven VLA post-training: a coding agent uses environment tools and execution feedback to write closed-loop code policies that generate demonstrations from states where a frozen VLA fails, then curates those trajectories for student post-training on LIBERO, MetaWorld and RoboCasa.
mechanism: Given a VLA checkpoint, a task specification and configured environment tools, Agentic-Teacher analyzes failed rollouts, selects intervention states, and iteratively develops closed-loop code policies through execution feedback. Validated policies become reusable demonstration generators that collect successful continuations from states where the VLA struggles. Trajectories are noised, idle-frame-filtered while preserving gripper transitions, and filtered with the frozen base model's flow-matching loss, then mixed with successful VLA rollouts for post-training so the updated policy runs without the coding agent.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): in simulation, post-training improves π0 success rates from 79.4% to 87.8% on LIBERO-10, from 80.4% to 90.6% on MetaWorld-10, and from 0% to 30.0% across three RoboCasa tasks. Numeric tables and baselines beyond the abstract unread.

title: Talk to Act: A Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Benchmark for Human Intent Extraction and Action Planning in Robotics
why: B-type conversational HRI benchmark: a synthetic multi-turn dialogue set annotated with action intents, object references and task plans, used to evaluate small open-weight LLMs on robotics intent extraction framed as tool-calling, without task-specific fine-tuning. No closed-loop robot execution is reported in the abstract.
mechanism: The dataset is synthetically generated and annotated with action intents, object references and task plans across scenarios and user personas. Intent extraction is framed as tool-calling, where each predicted action is a structured function call with arguments grounded in the dialogue. Models from 270M to 8B parameters are benchmarked zero-shot on intent extraction and action planning, aimed at local deployment.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): compact open-weight models achieve reasonable performance on the intent-extraction and action-planning task even at relatively small scales and without task-specific fine-tuning. Numeric tables unread. The abstract does not report closed-loop robot success. Comments: 6 pages, 4 figures; extended version of an ICRA 2026 MEI workshop paper.

title: Grounding Object-to-Object Hazard Reasoning into 3D Risk Fields for Task-Conditioned Safety
why: A-type safety harness around a VLM for manipulation: the model is given a structured safety tool on an RGB-D observation and a language task, rejects non-recoverable tasks or names preventable object-pair hazards, then grounds those constraints as 3D risk fields that correct nominal motions during execution.
mechanism: A VLM is provided with a structured safety tool over an RGB-D observation and a natural-language instruction. It first decides whether the task should be rejected as non-recoverably hazardous; otherwise it identifies preventable object-pair hazards and the spatial relations that must be avoided. Open-vocabulary segmentation and depth ground the objects in 3D and build continuous risk fields, which an obstacle-avoidance module uses to correct nominal robot motions during execution.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): the framework is evaluated on preventable hazards, tasks requiring rejection, and safe variants in simulation and the real world. Numeric tables and trial counts beyond the abstract unread.

title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
why: A-type language-instructed humanoid navigation stack with an agentic workflow (X-Navarch) that decomposes a brief instruction into sub-tasks and deploys a navigation model (MELIOR) for long-horizon indoor-to-outdoor missions, with closed-loop results on a Lingxi X2 and on R2R-CE / RxR-CE.
mechanism: X-Nav covers data collection in open-source scenes, digital twins and on-robot logs, plus a navigation model MELIOR that takes only RGB from the built-in camera (MELIOR-A predicts actions; MELIOR-N predicts a navigation goal). The agentic workflow X-Navarch turns a brief human instruction into sub-tasks and deploys MELIOR with explicit target navigation and obstacle avoidance. LiDAR and odometry are used for target approach and low-level control. The model is adapted with digital-twin data of the deployment site before the real-site run.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on the Lingxi X2, X-Nav completes a mission of about a hundred metres from an office lobby to a store in a neighbouring building, including a mid-mission destination change, a door crossing, and (with X-Navarch) static and dynamic obstacles. Twin adaptation is reported to raise closed-loop success in the twin before real-site deployment. MELIOR is also reported as competitive on R2R-CE and RxR-CE. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: A Generalizable Approach to Safety-Aware Robotic Behavior Planning with an Explicit Constraint Space
why: A-type safety layer for LLM/VLM tabletop behavior planning: an explicit Constraint Space of reusable textual safety rules is selected by a query-conditioned model, a multimodal Safety Inspector audits and corrects primitive plans, and validated feedback is used for test-time adaptation of applicability and of the inspector.
mechanism: Reusable textual safety rules live in an explicit Constraint Space. A lightweight query-conditioned dual-tower model selects constraints applicable to the current task and scene, which are passed with the original instruction and image to a multimodal behavior planner. A multimodal Safety Inspector evaluates generated primitive plans, reconstructs the applicable constraint set, and provides corrective planning feedback. Validated feedback is used for test-time adaptation of constraint applicability and for parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation of the inspector, and newly identified constraints are added to the Constraint Space.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): the paper presents the integrated framework (explicit safety knowledge, context-aware constraint selection, corrective inspection, and test-time knowledge adaptation) for safety-aware robotic behavior planning. Specific benchmarks, trial counts and success rates are not stated in the abstract. Numeric tables unread.

title: Evaluating Language Models as Spatial Priors for Object-Goal Navigation
why: B-type evaluation/audit of whether open-weight LLMs can supply a spatial placement prior for object-goal navigation, rather than only object–room associations; results are largely cautionary versus priors built from real layouts.
mechanism: The study asks two open-weight LLMs (Qwen3.5-27B and Gemma-4-31B-it) for a distribution over target position in a room, using real layouts from CubiCasa5K and ScanNet. It measures likelihoods on real versus perturbed layouts, inspects generated rooms, and compares searched area under the generated prior, a uniform prior, and a prior built from real layouts, including a spatially smoothed variant.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): generated rooms follow room-type object frequencies and sizes, but wall proximity does not follow real room-type differences. As a search prior, generated placements reduce searched area relative to a uniform prior by less than a third of the reduction from a real-layout prior, and by less than two thirds when both priors are spatially smoothed. The authors support LLMs for object–room associations and for writing coordinates under external constraints plus a geometric check, but not as placement priors where real layouts are available. Numeric tables unread.

title: ESI: An Embodied Self-Improvement Flywheel for LLM-VLA Agents
why: A-type embodied self-improvement loop for a modular LLM-VLA agent: environmental interaction is used to jointly refine the LLM's prompts, a shared skill interface, and VLA parameters so reasoning and action stay aligned, including recovery and handoff after corrections, evaluated closed-loop on RoboDojo.
mechanism: ESI treats the modular LLM-VLA agent as the unit of post-training. It repeatedly refines the prompts that guide the LLM, the shared skill interface that expresses intent, and the VLA parameters that realize that intent, then redeploys the components together. The LLM's subtask decisions provide semantic supervision for what the policy should execute; effective corrections and subsequent student continuations provide action-level supervision for recovery and handoff. The student also learns from its own effective execution, including when the overall episode fails. The abstract states that the agent does not generate task-specific control code.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on ten selected RoboDojo tasks, ESI achieves a mean Score of 62.03 and a mean success rate of 49.41%. On both metrics it is reported to outperform the published reference results of all compared hybrid embodied agents, including GO-3 Nano Preview (47.27 Score and 36.60% success), and all compared code-based methods. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: Objectives as Policies: Vision-Language Model Cost Programs for Contact-Rich Manipulation
why: A-type VLM-to-MPC harness for contact-rich manipulation: a pretrained VLM writes an editable objective program (staged costs plus completion conditions from a cost library) that a shared sampling-based MPC executes in a real-to-sim digital twin, with the program updated from rollouts before real-world deployment.
mechanism: Objectives as Policies (OaP) connects a pretrained VLM to a shared sampling-based MPC through an editable objective program. Each program specifies a sequence of stages, combining running and terminal costs from a cost library with stage completion conditions. Given a language instruction and a scene observation, a simulation-based digital twin is built via real-to-sim; the VLM generates the program, the MPC executes it in simulation, and the VLM iteratively updates the program from MPC rollouts before real-world deployment.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): evaluated in both simulation and the real world on four tabletop manipulation tasks, and reported to outperform strong baselines. Task names, trial counts and numeric success rates are not stated in the abstract. Tables unread.

title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
why: B-type navigation benchmark and VLM evaluation for accessibility-aware, embodiment-conditioned path selection (humanoid, quadruped, and people with visual or mobility impairments), with goal-reaching, collision-aware and accessibility-aligned metrics rather than goal-only scores.
mechanism: VLAN contains 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories and 160K keyframes with diverse lighting, semantics and path geometries. For each trajectory it provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments. Obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk and Blocked. Evaluation measures physical safety and alignment with user-specific constraints via goal-reaching, collision-aware and accessibility-aligned metrics. Modern vision-language models are benchmarked on the suite.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): benchmarked VLMs often fail to consistently adapt obstacle relevance, path selection and safety criteria across user profiles. The authors argue that accessibility-aware navigation needs dedicated datasets, tasks and metrics beyond conventional embodied navigation evaluation. Numeric model-by-model tables unread. Comments: accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track; 25 pages, 17 tables, 6 figures.

title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
why: B-type position and evaluation-framework paper for agentic robotics: it treats a foundation model plus an embodied harness as Embodied System 2, proposes measuring both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance, and sketches a roadmap from primitive execution to standing roles.
mechanism: The paper defines an agentic robotic system as applying a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks in a closed loop of observing, interpreting intent, reasoning, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes and adapting strategy. It argues that Embodied System 2 — a foundation model together with an embodied harness — is the decision-making core, and that the central challenge is translating general-purpose reasoning into verifiable actions under physical constraints (reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable change, irreversible consequences). It proposes an evaluation framework covering model capabilities and closed-loop system performance, and a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): this is a position, evaluation-framework and roadmap paper rather than a new closed-loop robot experiment. It claims that, within weeks of GPT-6 Astra, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. No new numeric tables are described in the abstract.

title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
why: A-type robot-use agent post-training: an open-weight 27B reasoning model is trained entirely in simulation with robot-use RL (RURL) via a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) to emit end-effector poses from a think-act loop, then transferred to a real dual-arm robot and evaluated on LIBERO, RoboDojo and LIBERO-Pro.
mechanism: The authors train a 27B open-weight reasoning model as a robot-use agent (RUA) with reinforcement learning entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. The model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose; the abstract describes this loop as operating without an additional harness. PEAR is used to run robot-use RL (RURL) on simulated robot tasks at scale. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the policy is evaluated on a real dual-arm robot, on LIBERO, and on LIBERO-Pro under changed task instructions in familiar scenes. Retention of general reasoning/coding/vision capabilities is also reported.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): after sim training on LIBERO and RoboDojo, the model succeeds in 60% of trials on a real dual-arm robot versus none for the base model. On LIBERO, success rises from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. On LIBERO-Pro, the model succeeds in 57.4% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene, versus 0.75% for a π0.5 VLA fine-tuned on demonstrations. No measurable degradation is reported on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. Numeric tables and trial counts beyond the abstract unread.
